bib.title: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways

question: What does scaling a dense decoder-only Transformer to 540B parameters and 780B tokens buy in few-shot performance across language, reasoning, code and multilingual tasks?
contributions: Efficient scaling with Pathways to 6144 TPU v4 chips

method.summary: Trains three dense decoder-only Transformers (8B, 62B, 540B) with the same recipe on a 780B-token (795B for 62B) single-epoch mixture, using Pathways across two TPU v4 pods with no pipeline parallelism, then evaluates few-shot on 29 English NLP tasks, BIG-bench, chain-of-thought reasoning, code (plus a code-finetuned PaLM-Coder), translation, multilingual generation/QA, memorization, contamination, bias and toxicity.

datasets.name: PaLM pretraining mixture
datasets.split: exactly one epoch, shuffled identically for all models
datasets.source: social media conversations 50%, filtered webpages 27%, books (English) 13%, GitHub code 5%, Wikipedia 4%, news (English) 1%; multilingual part spans over 100 languages; non-English about 22%
datasets.preprocessing: webpages sampled in proportion to a quality-classifier score; code filtered by licence (copyleft excluded), 24 languages, 196GB, deduplicated by Levenshtein distance; vocabulary generated from the training data

datasets.name: ExtraPythonData
datasets.source: GitHub repositories not used in pretraining

datasets.name: 29 English NLP benchmarks (TriviaQA, NQ, WebQ, LAMBADA, HellaSwag, StoryCloze, Winograd, WinoGrande, PIQA, ARC, OpenBookQA, DROP, CoQA, QuAC, SQuADv2, RACE, SuperGLUE, ANLI)
datasets.split: same splits as Du et al. (2021) and Brown et al. (2020)

datasets.name: BIG-bench
datasets.size: 150 text tasks (58 in common with Gopher/Chinchilla/GPT-3)

datasets.name: GSM8K, SVAMP, MAWPS, ASDiv, AQuA, CommonsenseQA, StrategyQA
datasets.split: 8-shot chain of thought, exemplars from Wei et al. 2022b

datasets.name: HumanEval, MBPP, GSM8K-Python, TransCoder (560 test samples), DeepFix (1260 programs)

models.name: PaLM 540B
models.architecture: decoder-only Transformer; SwiGLU, parallel layers, multi-query attention, RoPE, shared input-output embeddings, no biases
models.tokenizer: SentencePiece, lossless, digits split individually, unknown Unicode to UTF-8 bytes

models.name: PaLM 62B
models.architecture: decoder-only Transformer; SwiGLU, parallel layers, multi-query attention, RoPE, shared input-output embeddings, no biases
models.tokenizer: SentencePiece, lossless, digits split individually, unknown Unicode to UTF-8 bytes

other.train_tokens: 795B (an oversight in checkpoint selection; also continued to 1325B in Appendix F)

models.name: PaLM 8B
models.architecture: decoder-only Transformer; SwiGLU, parallel layers, multi-query attention, RoPE, shared input-output embeddings, no biases
models.tokenizer: SentencePiece, lossless, digits split individually, unknown Unicode to UTF-8 bytes

other.finetune: stage 1 6.5B tokens: 60% Python (ExtraPythonData), 30% multi-language code, 10% natural language; stage 2 1.9B tokens more Python; 7.75B finetuning tokens total, 5.9B Python

models.name: GPT-3 175B, Gopher 280B, Chinchilla 70B, Megatron-Turing NLG 530B, GLaM 64B/64E, LaMDA 137B, Codex 12B, Davinci Codex

training.objective: standard language modeling loss (average log probability of all tokens, no label smoothing) plus auxiliary z-loss 1e-4 * log^2 Z
training.optimizer: Adafactor without factorization (Adam with parameter scaling), beta1 0.9, beta2 = 1.0 - k^-0.8, global-norm gradient clipping 1.0
training.lr_schedule: constant 1e-2 for the first 10,000 steps, then decay 1/sqrt(k) with step k
training.batch_size: 540B: 512 (1M tokens) until step 50k, 1024 (2M) until step 115k, 2048 (4M) until step 255k; smaller models followed similar schedules
training.weight_decay: dynamic, lr^2.0 (lr is the current learning rate)
training.dropout: 0 in pretraining; 0.1 for finetuning in most cases
training.regularisation: no biases; z-loss; kernel init N(0, 1/sqrt(n_in)), embeddings N(0,1), pre-softmax logits scaled by 1/sqrt(n)
training.hardware: 540B: 6144 TPU v4 chips (two pods of 3072, 768 hosts each), 12-way model parallel x 256-way fully sharded data parallel per pod, two-way pod-level data parallel via Pathways, no pipeline parallelism
training.compute: 2.56e24 train FLOPs (540B, excluding rematerialization), 3.08e23 (62B), 4.29e22 (8B); 29600 PetaFLOP/s-days for 540B
training.wall_clock: 6144 TPU v4 chips for 1200 hours plus 3072 chips for 336 hours, including some downtime and repeated steps

other.loss_spikes: about 20 spikes in 540B, none in smaller models; mitigated by restarting from a checkpoint about 100 steps before the spike and skipping 200-500 batches
other.bitwise_determinism: fully reproducible from any checkpoint (JAX+XLA+T5X, deterministic data pipeline)
other.finetune_superglue: lr 5e-5, Adafactor, batch 32, converges typically in under 15K steps
other.energy: 271.43 tCO2e, Oklahoma datacenter PUE 1.08, 378.5W per TPU v4 chip, 89% carbon-free energy

inference.decoding: greedy for Figure 1 and pass@1 code; nucleus sampling p=0.95 temperature 0.8 for pass@k with k>1; top-k 40 temperature 1.0 for toxicity
inference.samples: 25 continuations for each of 10K prompts (toxicity); pass@k with k samples per problem (code)
inference.prompting: 0/1/few-shot with number of shots per task in Table 4; 8-shot chain of thought exemplars from Wei et al. 2022b; 5-shot BIG-bench and MMLU; 2-shot exemplars for Fig 1

parameters.calculator: post-hoc external calculator on arithmetic datasets, said not to improve any dataset by more than 5%
parameters.contamination_threshold: example is contaminated if at least 70% of its 8-grams in question, prompt or target appear in training data

other.memorization_probe: 100 token spans from training examples, first 50 tokens as prompt, greedy, exact match of 50-token continuation

metrics.name: model FLOPs utilization (MFU)
metrics.definition: observed tokens/sec over theoretical max tokens/sec at peak FLOPs, counting only forward+backward FLOPs, not rematerialization: R = P / (6N + 12LHQT)

metrics.name: few-shot accuracy / EM / F1 per task
normalized preferred metric (BIG-bench)
metrics.definition: random chance = 0, max = 100 for multiple choice, averaged over tasks

metrics.name: pass@k (code)
metrics.definition: percentage of k samples that solve the task (not the Chen et al. estimator)

metrics.name: memorization rate
metrics.definition: fraction of 100 sampled training spans whose 50-token continuation is reproduced exactly given the first 50 tokens

limits: No ablation separates model size from tokens or data quality; the authors say a 62B model on 7T tokens versus 540B on 780B is an open question (Sec 13).
Only three scales (8B, 62B, 540B), so the discontinuity analysis rests on three points.
Single run per configuration, no seeds or confidence intervals; WebQuestions 1-shot varies across checkpoints 2B tokens apart.
Parallel layers had a small quality drop at 8B and were assumed neutral at 540B by extrapolation.
Loss spikes had no principled fix; the restart-and-skip strategy was empirical.
Bias and toxicity analyses are English only, template-based and brittle to prompt wording; Perspective API has its own bias.
Code correctness is measured on a small number of tests and can overestimate performance.
Davinci Codex comparison is not controlled: size, data and post-processing unknown.
Data repeats in some subcorpora beyond 780B tokens, which is why training stopped there.
Dated: BIG-bench comparisons use the GPT-3 models from the GPT-3 paper, not newer OpenAI models.
